hero.headline: Open Source Architect building light, sustainable developer infrastructure and local-first CI/CD automation.
hero.sub: I maintain three open-source tools: a local gate that runs your CI before you push, a dependency-free process that stands in for third-party payment and identity APIs, and an air-gapped automation engine that runs enterprise workflows without a network. All three publish their measurements, and all three publish the claims they do not make.
hero.scrollHint: Case studies, writing and public evidence

positioning.statement: I build the unglamorous layer of developer infrastructure: the tools that decide whether a team waits forty seconds or forty minutes for a green build, and the services that keep an enterprise running when the network does not. My work is open source, benchmarked in public, and written up in full — including the measurements I threw away and the claims I do not make. Infrastructure claims are worth exactly what the evidence behind them is worth, so the evidence ships with the tool.
supports: Every product I ship is published as open source, with the harness that produced its measurements included, so the claims are reproducible — and with a documented section on what is not claimed.
Case studies lead with the failure mode and the before/after numbers, not the feature list. Where a number is unflattering, it stays.
The same discipline applies to the systems I build for enterprises: data-driven configuration, explicit audit trails, and a safe path out when a component is unreachable.

specialisms.title: Developer Experience (DX)
specialisms.body: Removing the wall between an edit and the signal that says whether the edit was right. Most of it is determinism: the same script has to run on the laptop and on the runner, so there is one copy of the setup rather than two implementations that drift.

specialisms.title: Local-First & Air-Gapped Systems
specialisms.body: Systems that keep working when the network does not. Mocks that answer a payment API without a key, a local model that classifies intent without a cloud gateway, and an audit trail that stays queryable on the host it was written on.

specialisms.title: Platform & Service Engineering
specialisms.body: Windows services, runspace pools, transactional persistence, plug-in extension points, RBAC and break-glass recovery. The unglamorous layer that decides whether a platform is operable by one person or by a rota.

specialisms.title: Green Container Tooling
specialisms.body: Tooling that is light by default: small memory footprints, zero idle CPU, and a deliberate bias toward doing less work on the developer's machine rather than more work on someone's metered runner. The footprint is enforced as a build gate, not asserted in a README.

principles.title: Measure, then claim
principles.body: A benchmark is a product with a maintenance burden. I publish the harness alongside the result so a reader can re-run it and disagree with me — and I publish the measurement I threw away, because a reader who knows the spread can trust the number.

principles.title: State what you do not claim
principles.body: Every evidence document I write has a section listing what is not claimed. A tool that overclaims about speed is a tool that has to be defended, and the defence is always weaker than the original claim would have been.

principles.title: Configuration is data, not code
principles.body: A workflow declared as a JSON blueprint can be reviewed, diffed, audited and replayed. A workflow expressed as a controller method can only be changed by a deploy — and a deploy is the wrong tool for a business rule.

principles.title: Degrade, do not depend
principles.body: If a component is unreachable, the system has to have a defined fallback and a defined audit record of having used it. A local model with a deterministic fallback beats a cloud model with a timeout.

timeline.title: Open Source Architect
timeline.body: Maintaining CI Kit, api-mock-services and the air-gapped automation engine; writing about CI/CD drift, local-first infrastructure and reproducible measurement.

timeline.title: Platform / DevEx Engineering
timeline.body: Owned the internal CI platform and developer onboarding for payment-product teams. The workspace these tools came from had 28 red runs in a row and nobody could tell that the jobs had never started — which is what turned a local gate from a convenience into the answer to 'did I break something?'

timeline.title: Backend / Infrastructure Engineer
timeline.body: Service and infrastructure work across Go, Python and Node services, with a gradual drift toward build tooling, container images and everything that sits between the laptop and the cluster. The Docker and infrastructure-as-code writing from this period is in the earlier archive.

timeline.body: Application support, service desk and delivery work before and alongside engineering — the period in which I learned to read logs, reproduce faults and write the documentation that made a system survivable by the next person. The 2013–2025 archive is an honest record of that arc.
